ai.description: This 3–4 cm frog has a globular body with a marbled brown and cream pattern. It features a distinct, narrow snout and lacks webbing on the toes. It belongs to the family Microhylidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uperodon variegatus* is best distinguished by the distinct, irregular white or yellowish spots scattered across its dark, brownish-grey dorsal skin.
ai.habitat: *Uperodon variegatus* inhabits dry deciduous forests, scrublands, and agricultural areas across the Indian subcontinent, typically at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Eluru Dot Frog is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time buried underground to escape the heat, emerging mainly during heavy monsoon rains.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uperodon variegatus* breeds during the monsoon, laying large clutches of up to 2,000 eggs in temporary rain pools. It is an explosive breeder with aquatic larvae.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Eluru Dot Frog is endemic to peninsular India, primarily occurring in the Eastern Ghats and coastal Andhra Pradesh at low to moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Eluru Dot Frog emits a high-pitched, rapid series of metallic "peep-peep" notes, typically heard from shallow, rain-filled pools in scrub forests and grasslands.
